column2: Maybe the killer had gotten into the inn long before.
And then took plenty of time to cut up Mr. Tanaka's body...
Otherwise there's no explaining how a person could be taken apart like that.
Or is there some other way?
In the short time between the sound of the window breaking and our rushing over, a way to dispose of a body...
There's no way.
The killer must have slipped into the inn well before that.
But when, exactly?
From where?
How could anyone have gotten into the inn without being noticed?
Since everything was properly locked up, the only ways in were the front entrance and the drying room door.
But anyone coming through either would surely have been seen.
Besides, even if all the guests were in the back, at least Mr. Kobayashi can always tell who comes and goes.
Which means...
Came in the front, unseen.
I see...
I saw the truth.
I'm not about to claim the killer was an invisible man.
The killer's figure was perfectly visible to all of us.
And yet, he'd been in a psychological blind spot.
“What's wrong?
You look like a pigeon that got hit with a water pistol.”
{n2} looked at me and laughed.
“You mean a pea shooter.”
“Who cares, same thing.
So what is it?”
“I figured out the truth.
Who the killer is in the dismemberment murder.”
Everyone looked at me with a start.
really?”
Mr. Kobayashi was shocked too.
“The killer...
You're not saying it's someone we know, are you?”
{n2} asked fearfully.
“...I'm afraid so.”
“No way...”
I said.
“The killer is...
me.”
“What?!”
Everyone's jaws dropped.
They looked too shocked to say anything.
Naturally.
Even I, the one who said it, was shocked.
You, what on earth...{r}{p}Is that true?
If so, why? And how,
when...?”
{n2} asked haltingly.
“Well...”
“What do you mean, 'well'...
you?”
Mr. Kobayashi looked at me suspiciously.
“Ain't it you who did it, huh?”
Mr. Kayama glared at me, irritated.
“You just said the killer was you, right?”
Toshio pressed.
“No, I mean...”
As I flailed, Mr. Kayama shot me a glare.
“You mean what?{r}{p}Spit it out, if yer a man!”
“Well...”
Why did I say that I was the killer?
Anyway, I had to smooth this over somehow, or I'd really end up being pinned as the killer...
“No, what I meant to say was this.{r}{p}Okay?”
I cleared my throat.
“The killer is me...
is the one thing that's absolutely impossible.”
Everyone fell over.
“What kind of thing is that?!”
“Don't say confusing stuff!”
Stop dating a guy like this.”
“He was never my fiancé to begin with.”
They tore me to shreds.
I told everyone in a loud voice.
“I was going to follow that with the real killer's name.{r}{p}You all just jumped to conclusions!”
“Then who's the real killer?”
“That's...”
I had to somehow salvage my honor here...
“The killer is {n2}.
You.”
{n2} looked at me in shock.
Are you serious?”
She glared at me with a ferocious look.
“Uh,
er,
As I stammered, {n2} blew up at me.
“That's impossible!
We were together the whole time!”
right...
Sorry, I take it back.”
I withdrew my deduction without a fight.
“If you're going to talk nonsense, be quiet.”
“This time I'm serious...
I really reasoned it out...”
“Then who?”
“The real killer is...”
“The killer is, of course, neither me nor {n2}...”
With the banana trick...
If I applied the banana trick...
That's the one where you peel it and it's mysteriously already sliced into rounds.
That trick uses a needle and thread.
From outside the peel, you use a needle to run thread around only the banana inside, then pull hard.
Say you wrap something thin and strong, like piano wire, around the unconscious Mr. Tanaka's body.
Then you pass the end out through the gap of the closed window and tie it to the back of a car.
Then you drive the car off.
Mr. Tanaka's body slams into the window frame and stops, but the car keeps going.
The piano wire bites into the flesh with brutal force,
and the next instant his body falls to pieces...
Impossible...
That can't happen.
No matter what, piano wire couldn't cut so cleanly through bone.
Besides, the window had already been open, so it would be odd for the whole dismembered body to be inside the room.
I discarded the silly idea.
When the window broke, there was exactly one person who wasn't in the lounge.
I remember now.
What if the room itself had a mechanism...
When Mr. Tanaka lay on the bed, a switch would flip automatically.
Something like metal belts would strap his body to the bed.
And a rotating saw blade would come down from the ceiling, screaming...
No good...
That's like James Bond caught in a trap.
If by some remote chance this fantasy were right, the culprits could only be the Kobayashis, the owners of the building.
But I couldn't imagine they had any motive for this.
Besides, done this way the whole room would be drenched in blood, and the bed would at least be somewhat slashed up.
I discarded the silly idea.
When the window broke, there was one person who wasn't in the lounge!
The basement!
They dug in from underground!
“The cellar!”
I stood up.
“What, all of a sudden?
What about the cellar?”
{n2} asked in surprise.
“I figured out how the killer got in!{r}{p}The cellar!
They dug a tunnel and got into the cellar!”
“The cellar?
...But the door leading down is locked from this side.{r}{p}Even if someone got into the wine cellar below, they couldn't get in here.”
Mr. Kobayashi objected.
“But a wine cellar lock is an old-fashioned kind, isn't it?{r}{p}Like a stick with a few bumps on it...{r}{p}Anyone with a bit of skill could open it with a hairpin or something.”
Of course I couldn't, but surely there were people who could.
“True, it's not much of a lock, but...”
“Anyway, let's check.”
At my words, Mr. Kobayashi reluctantly agreed.
Mr. Kobayashi unlocked the door to the basement, and I peered down the dark stairs.
A slightly damp, cold air seemed to rise up.
When he touched the switch on the wall, a light came on below.
Having raised the idea, I couldn't very well not go down first.
I gulped and descended the stairs one step at a time.
Though it was a wine cellar, it didn't smell of wine; it smelled like a used bookstore.
At the bottom of the stairs, in the bleak light of a bare bulb, I saw rows of dusty wine racks.
“There's a hole somewhere in this wall.”
I said to Mr. Kobayashi and the others coming down behind me.
“Here?
...A hole?”
Mr. Kobayashi swung his head around and spoke in a doubtful voice.
“Let's split up and search.{r}{p}I'll go around from the right, and Mr. Kobayashi, please take the left.”
{n2}, Mr. Kayama, and the others who had followed behind waited breathlessly at the foot of the stairs.
Apparently they had decided to watch us search.
Rapping the wooden wall with my fist, I carefully searched from top to bottom.
When I reached the far end after going halfway around, Mr. Kobayashi was standing there looking sour.
“Find anything?”
“...What about you, Mr. Kobayashi?”
He silently shook his head.
“That can't be...
You did check properly, didn't you?”
“If you don't believe me, check for yourself.”
Mr. Kobayashi retorted, a little irritated.
It wasn't that I distrusted Mr. Kobayashi, but I couldn't help checking.
I rapped the wall even more carefully than before, going around to check for suspicious seams or spots that sounded odd.
Back at the stairs, I went around a second time.
There was nothing out of the ordinary.
“No way...”
I stood there in disbelief.
So nobody could have gotten in from outside after all...
Was that it?
But then, the killer could only be someone among us!
Yet we had all been in the lounge when it happened...
Everyone went back to the lounge, muttering what sounded like complaints about me.
Mr. Kobayashi and {n2} also shot me reproachful looks.
It made me feel even worse that Kyoko made fresh coffee again to replace the stone-cold cups.
Kyoko came back once more and began pouring coffee for everyone.
By then, I had managed to pull myself together somewhat.
Wait a minute...
When that window broke, not everyone had been in the lounge...
I suddenly realized it.
He was killed from outside.
What in a detective novel they'd call a remote killing.
But how could you chop up a person standing far away?
I thought desperately.
Right, the window had been open.
A weapon that could cut up Mr. Tanaka, standing at the window, from a distance...
That's it,
a laser beam!
Laser scalpels had been in practical use for years.
It wouldn't be strange if a far more powerful version had been secretly developed!
...No, that is odd.
Realistically, I couldn't imagine anyone going to the trouble of using such a grand weapon in a place like this.
Besides, even if they had, there should be traces left on a wall or something.
So the killer did get inside after all...
But there was no way in.
Which means...
the killer was one of us.
